clue.text: So dish may appear very hot, on the surface

definitions.text: So dish may appear very hot, on the surface

parts.words: So dish may appear very hot, on the surface
parts.note: a dish set alight with brandy at the table looks fiercely hot, with flames playing over its surface

explanation.surface: A warning that a dish may look scalding on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served flambé is doused in spirit and ignited, so flames dance over its surface.

clue.text: Charge restricting free trade? Form an alliance

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: free means released from its order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tariff that hampers free trade between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like half of the phrase 'free trade', but it is the anagram signal; 'restricting' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is for states or groups to unite under a central authority, forming an alliance.

clue.text: Beard a heartless woman

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman with no heart grows facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: An awn is a bristle on an ear of barley or other grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The bristly hairs on ears of grain are collectively called the beard.

clue.text: In the course of puzzling, plot to include inspirational one

indicators.note: to include means one piece holds the other

parts.note: a plot of garden is a bed
a muse is a source of inspiration

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a story that brings in a source of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bemused means being puzzled or bewildered, the state one is in while puzzling.

clue.text: What poet did to be calm

definitions.meaning: a poet writes, that is, puts verses together

explanation.definitionFit: A poet composes verse, and composed also means collected or unruffled.

clue.text: How one side's fielders hope to achieve dismissals?

definitions.text: How one side's fielders hope to achieve dismissals?

parts.words: How one side's fielders hope to achieve dismissals?
parts.note: in cricket the off side is one half of the field, and fielders there hope a catching opportunity comes their way

explanation.surface: Cricket fielders on one side of the pitch hoping to get batsmen out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the 'off' side is one half of the field, and a catch offered is a 'chance'. The phrase usually means in the slight hope.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting in the slender hope that something might happen.

clue.text: Indian bread torn apart — have half?

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters are rearranged
half means only the first two of the four letters are used

explanation.surface: Someone rips a piece of Indian bread and offers half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' rearranges APART into PARAT; 'half' takes HA from HAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratha is a flaky, layered flatbread from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Annual chore to be done well — start to compile list

parts.note: a spring is a well, a source of water

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: to list is to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A yearly household task that should be done thoroughly, beginning with a checklist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like part of 'done well' but is a noun, a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring-cleaning is the thorough annual cleaning of a home, a chore traditionally done each spring.

clue.text: Resolutely apply incomplete study on polling system

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a den is a private study
a vote is the system of polling opinion

explanation.surface: An unfinished study is put to work on how elections are run.
explanation.definitionFit: To devote oneself to something is to dedicate time and effort to it with resolve.

clue.text: Lower number used moderation, with new rioting

indicators.note: letters running riot are thrown into disorder, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A minority used moderation even when the new rioting broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' shuffles MODERATION plus N into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction the denominator is the figure written underneath, hence the lower number.

clue.text: Gun found by clergyman

definitions.meaning: to gun an engine is to ... it hard
The short form of Reverend, a title for a member of the clergy

explanation.definitionFit: To rev is to gun a motor, and Rev abbreviates Reverend, a clergyman's title.

clue.text: An option is genuine — almost join in

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: genuine means real

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to fuse is to join together

explanation.surface: A choice that is really on offer, nearly joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims FUSE to FUS, which goes 'in' REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: First refusal is the right to buy before anyone else, so a refusal can be an option.

clue.text: Chap trapping one wild animal having charges dismissed?

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: Fred is a typical man's name, standing for any chap

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig, an animal

explanation.surface: A man has caught a dangerous beast and the charges against him are dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' seems to describe the animal but is the anagram signal for 'one'; 'trapping' is the container. Free on board is a shipping term where the seller covers loading costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Under a free-on-board contract the seller pays the shipping costs, so the buyer has no loading charges.

clue.text: Instant, in the past, when 20 struck

definitions.text: Instant, in the past, when 20 struck

parts.words: Instant, in the past, when 20 struck
parts.note: 'instant' in old letter-writing means this current month; here it is a date long ago on which the man at 20 down stabbed Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A moment from history when someone delivered a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like 'a moment'; it is the old commercial abbreviation 'inst.', meaning this month. 20 down is BRUTUS, one of Caesar's assassins on 15 March 44 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was assassinated on 15 March, a date the Roman calendar called the Ides.

clue.text: Aussie's. state of obsession, after job's unfinished

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first
unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a task is a job
mania is an obsession

explanation.surface: An obsessive state sets in once a job is left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an island state of Australia.

clue.text: Doing fairly well in French

parts.note: the French idiom for so-so or middling, describing someone getting along tolerably

explanation.surface: A school report on a pupil's modest progress in French lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pupil's grade in French; the answer is the French phrase meaning 'so-so'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally says 'like this, like that', meaning tolerable or middling.

clue.text: Some old soldiers got me to adopt plan I devised

indicators.note: to adopt means to take in, so one piece holds the other
devised means worked out anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take up a plan they devised themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' is the anagram signal and 'to adopt' the container; 'got' is a link. A maniple was a company in the Roman legion.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniple was a subdivision of a Roman legion, a body of old soldiers.

clue.text: A certain element seen to become increasingly heated

definitions.meaning: a particular chemical element, the liquid metal Hg
the liquid metal in a thermometer rises visibly as the temperature climbs

explanation.definitionFit: The quicksilver in a thermometer climbs as it warms, so its rise shows growing heat.

clue.text: Plant an oribi chewed

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small antelope munching on vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: An oribi is a small African antelope; 'chewed' rearranges AN ORIBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinia is a genus of trees, such as the false acacia or black locust.

clue.text: A word initially coined by a pal, Mike

parts.note: a crony is a close pal
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone credits a friend called Mike with inventing a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made from the first letters of other words is literally coined from initials.

clue.text: Drink with a meal

definitions.meaning: a cup of the hot beverage made from leaves
in Britain, a light afternoon or early evening meal

explanation.definitionFit: Tea is both a common hot drink and, in British usage, an evening meal.

clue.text: At first, pressing on it can stir, but should be restricted

definitions.text: At first, pressing on it can stir, but should be restricted

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the next word is used
being restricted means held in, so the word but is enclosed by the stirred letters
to stir is to mix up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pressing an alarm can cause a stir, so access to it should be limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is the anagram signal and 'should be restricted' the container; the whole clue also describes the device, which is why access to one is limited.
explanation.definitionFit: A panic button, when pressed, raises an alarm and stirs people into action, so its use should be restricted.

clue.text: Exploit unfinished recording

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A partly done recording is put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a resource is to exploit or draw on it.

clue.text: Without warning, in south of France, refuse to stock line

parts.note: sud is French for south

indicators.note: to stock means to hold within, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: to refuse is to deny

explanation.surface: A rubbish problem on the Riviera arrives out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of France' is the French word for south, not a region. 'to stock' puts L inside DENY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done suddenly happens abruptly, with no warning given.

clue.text: Lack of insight in my work -— first class gone west

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: A1 means first class, its figure one written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone laments a lack of vision in their work, with first-rate quality lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone west' means A1 is read backwards, giving IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is short-sightedness, used figuratively for a lack of foresight or insight.
